newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Wednesday:

Spokesman Thierry Daman said Commission President Jacques Santer and Bulgarian President Petar Stoyanov would be available for questions and photographs at the Breydel's VIP corner around 1300/1200 GMT on Thursday.
He said a compilation of the European Coal and Steel Community's archives would be presented at 1100/1000 GMT on the Breydel's 16th floor.

Daman said journalists were invited to the signature of the financing convention on the Asia initiative for reproductive health by Commissioner Manuel Marin and United Nations Deputy-Secretary General Nafis Sadik at 1100/1000 GMT on Thursday on the Breydel's 11th floor, room 126.
He said the news conference marking the opening of the launch of the "Year against racism and xenophobia" would be at 1730/1630 GMT on Thursday in The Hague.

Daman said the Commission had decided, during its weekly meeting, to propose three fines against Germany and two fines against Italy for non-application of EU environment legislation, on the basis of article 171 of the EU Treaty. He said it had also adopted a draft directive on telecoms taxation policy, a communication on environmental taxes and charges and structural funds programmes for French Aquitaine and for Germany.

Spokesman Nicolaas Wegter briefed on Bulgarian President Petar Soyanov's visit to the Commission on Thursday. He said he would meet President Jacques Santer and Commissioner Hans van den Broek in the morning.

In answer to a question, Daman said there were between 20 and 30 cases, including the five already decided upon, where the Commission could propose fines for non-application of EU legislation by Member States.
In answer to a question a Commission official briefed on the proposition for a new telecoms taxation policy.

Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas briefed on the orientation debate on the 1998 budget. He said the Commission would have to maintain an austerity policy and not exceed a total budget increase of three percent, bearing in mind that the structural funds budget increase alone was fixed at eight percent.
He also briefed on the orientation debate on the environmental responsibilities and announced a white paper on the issue to be presented soon.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/65: Commission supports industrial restructuring in Aquitaine.
- IP/97/66: Commission authorizes Ecu 806 million for industrial areas in Germany.
- IP/97/67: Commission proposes to modify the telecoms VAT policy.
- IP/97/68: Europe against AIDS: the fight goes on.
- IP/97/69: Commission approves the acquisition by TRW of Magna automotive holding (Germany) GmbH.
- IP/97/70: Environmental taxes and charges: the Commission presents guidelines for their efficient use in the single market.
- Memo/97/9: EU/Bulgaria relations.
- Memo/97/10: EU-Australia relations.
- Oil bulletin No 853.
